ai.title: CLI logs conversation summaries and adds opt-in trace writer
ai.summary: The CLI now writes a summary-only run config from `use-send-message.ts` and a summary-only agent step log in `run-agent-step.ts`, instead of dumping the full conversation history and attachments into `log.jsonl` on every step. It adds `trimOversizedChatLogs` (invoked via `setTimeout` at startup in `index.tsx`), which reclaims disk by deleting any `log.jsonl` over `MAX_LOG_FILE_BYTES` (10 MB) from chats untouched for more than `MIN_LOG_AGE_MS` (14 days). A new opt-in `TraceWriter` records message histories to `trace.jsonl` only when `CODEBUFF_TRACE` is set (or in dev), and the SDK's `getAgentRuntimeImpl` and `CodebuffClient` now accept a `traceWriter` option threaded through the agent runtime. Together these changes stop multi-GB debug logs while keeping detailed tracing available on demand.

facts: Follow redirects manually so every hop is re-validated against the SSRF policy, a public URL must not be able to 30x its way to an internal one.
Normalize IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) so they are classified by their embedded IPv4 range rather than as generic IPv6.
Throws an {@link SsrfError} if the URL is not safe to fetch from the server: non-http(s) schemes, IP literals in a private/reserved range, or hostnames that resolve to such a range.

IP literals are always checked synchronously (no DNS needed). Hostname resolution is performed via `lookupHost` unless `resolveDns` is false, this lets callers that supply their own `fetch` (e.g. unit tests with stubbed responses) skip the network lookup while still rejecting literal addresses.

ai.title: SDK read-url adds SSRF protection with manual redirect validation
ai.summary: New ssrf.ts module enforces SSRF policies for read-url by validating URL schemes, IP literals, and resolved hostnames against private/reserved ranges. read-url.ts now follows redirects manually (max 5 hops) to re-validate each target, replacing native fetch redirect handling. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) are normalized to their embedded IPv4 range for accurate classification. Callers can inject lookupHost or set resolveDns: false to skip DNS resolution while still blocking IP-literal targets.

eli5.text: When you ask the tool to read a web page, it now checks every link it's about to follow to make sure it's not secretly pointing at a private or internal address instead of a legitimate public site. Previously, a malicious page could use a chain of redirects to trick the tool into reaching internal-only addresses; now each redirect hop is validated, and addresses like 127.0.0.1 or localhost are always blocked. If a URL is rejected for these security reasons, you'll see an error message indicating the fetch was denied rather than returning any page content.

ai.summary: This release aggregates all user-visible updates since 1.0.680 into the published 1.0.681 CLI. DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID was bumped twice, landing on MiniMax M3 (`fireworks/deepseek-v4-flash` excluded from free pick), and the DeepSeek V4 Flash default switch for freebuff.com/chat now targets Fireworks inference. You can now use built-in web research that fetches and cites multiple sources before answering, plus a new chat agent that can spawn a web researcher to find current information. Insertion-order (FIFO) eviction so the cache can't grow without bound in long-lived processes (e.g. the freebuff chat server, which runs the agent runtime in-process). Templates are large, prompts plus handleSteps source.

ai.title: Fix agent runtime state leak on abort, bound SDK agent cache
ai.summary: Added clearProgrammaticRunState in packages/agent-runtime/src/run-programmatic-step.ts to release generator, STEP_ALL flag, and proposed file content on abort/error exits, not just endTurn. Wrapped loopAgentSteps in packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts with finally block calling this cleanup. Replaced unbounded Map with BoundedAgentCache (200 entries, FIFO eviction) in sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts to prevent memory growth in long-lived processes.

eli5.text: Today's update fixes a behind-the-scenes memory issue that could slow down or destabilize the agent runtime used by the freebuff chat server and other long-lived processes. Sometimes when a chat session was interrupted or errored out, the system forgot to clean up the internal state (the generator object, flags, and proposed file content) for that run, causing it to linger in memory indefinitely. The fix now ensures that cleanup happens every time a run's loop exits, including on aborts and errors, not just on normal completion. Additionally, the agent cache that stores large prompt templates has been capped at 200 entries with FIFO eviction, preventing unbounded memory growth in long-running sessions. These changes are internal stability improvements with no direct user-facing behavior
